newsitem.title: CANADA: Newfoundland says Terra Nova oil means new era.
newsitem.headline: Newfoundland says Terra Nova oil means new era.

text.p: The proposed 100,000 barrel per day Terra Nova oil project off the coast of Newfoundland represents the beginning of an industry fueled without government handouts, Brian Tobin, premier of the Canadian province, said on Thursday.

Tobin, speaking in the provincial capital of St. John's, conceded that every well drilled to date on the Grand Banks and the massive Hibernia project, slated to begin production in late 1997, had been partly financed by taxpayers' dollars.

"We're seeing a real point of departure from Hibernia, from one project constructed through a series of financial instruments involving government to an industry which is 100 percent sustained by the private sector," Tobin told reporters in a conference call following Petro-Canada's announcement on Thursday of several developments regarding Terra Nova and Newfoundland's fledgling oil industry.
The company's announcements come on the heels of several recent developments pointing to brisk oil activity in the region following the setting this year of new industry-friendly royalty terms.

Terra Nova, which is estimated to harbor 400 million barrels of reserves, would be developed using a steel monohull floating production facility in contrast to Hibernia's massive concrete gravity base structure. Estimated pre-production costs are C$1.6 billion.

Norm McIntyre, head of Petro-Canada's resources division, said the floating production facility represented the best technological solution for the stormy North Atlantic and could be completed at the lowest cost in the shortest timeframe.
Petro-Canada, operator of the Terra Nova project which is located 350 km southeast of St. John's, said it has closed its previously announced alliance with Norway's Norsk Hydro.
The deal involved the swapping of several offshore Newfoundland interests held by Petro-Canada for Norsk Hydro assets in the Norwegian sector of the North Sea.
Petro-Canada also said it picked a consortium called the Grand Banks Alliance, comprising of several international contractors, to develop Terra Nova's production facility.

"It has the added advantages of not only having substantial deck load capacity but very significant internal storage. We will have capacity for some 850,000 barrels of oil within the ship-shaped vessel," McIntyre said.
The Grand Banks Alliance is led by AGRA Industries Ltd, Brown & Root Inc, a a unit of Halliburton Co.

McIntyre said Terra Nova, whose partners are expected to decide on final go-ahead in the third quarter of 1997, would create up to 800 direct jobs in its pre-production phase and up to 500 longer term jobs.
Terra Nova's partners include Petro-Canada, Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada, Husky Oil Ltd, Norsk Hydro, Murphy Oil Corp and Mosbacher Operating Ltd.

Petro-Canada also said on Thursday it would expand its corporate office in St. John's and the company's vice-president of frontier and offshore operations would be permanently located in Newfoundland. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
